newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES SLIP 0.39 PCT IN THIN VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES SLIP 0.39 PCT IN THIN VOLUME.

text.p: Istanbul shares inched down in weaker volume and bearish sentiment on Monday due to lack of market-moving earnings forecasts and liquidity inflow, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 2,032, down eight points, or 0.39 percent from Friday. It moved in a tight range between 2,019 and 2,049 during the day.
Trade volume shrank 27.6 percent to 13.23 trillion lira ($81 million) on Monday, from Friday's 18.29 trillion.

Brokers said the market was likely to continue its sideways trade, slightly easing in the week as there would be no further predictions for first half company earnings which will be completed by the weekend.

"There was not any cash inflow to the market which needs the leadership of a sector or share to get a boost. Otherwise, 2,070 and 2,150 are stiff resistance levels, difficult to be pierced with the current transaction volume," said Neslihan Kacamak from Bab Securities.
"Within the week, a movement may begin in the energy or banking sectors," she said.

Of the 250 shares traded, losers outdid gainers by 118 to 80 and 52 ended stable. The IMKB Industrial eased 0.41 percent to 1,961, the IMKB Services fell 0.6 percent to 1,984 and the IMKB Financial dropped 0.45 percent to 2,203.

The top actives were largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, steady at 28,000 lira, followed by two real estate investment trusts -- Alarko, up 600 lira at 7,500 and Vakif, steady at 8,900 lira. They made up 10.1 percent of the total turnover.
Kacamak said expectations that returns on real estate investment trusts would rise parallel to the dollar's gains against the Turkish lira sparked activity in their shares.
